thread:
mira: Quick follow-up after the RFC thread: do we want nuance flags glued to pins or pulled from a separate timeline when resolving model refs? Thinking about canary rollouts + later rebinds.

liam: Separate timeline. If flags live on the pin we end up duplicating state on every pointer change. Timeline keeps the signal single-source and lets pointer moves be cheap.

sofia: Agree. Two constraints: (1) runtime must be able to atomically get the effective model_ref + timeline cursor so we don't mix flags from two different pointer generations; (2) timeline reads need to be cheap.

mira: For the atomicity piece I'm imagining a resolver API that returns a tiny struct: `model_ref`, `pointer_id`, `timeline_token`. The runtime caches that tuple.

liam: Yes. `timeline_token` should be an opaque monotonic string (like `tl-20260305-00042`) so caches can invalidate by token change. No client should parse it.

sofia: Tenant scoping: timeline entries must include a selector. We need exact-tenant, tag-based, and percentage buckets. Keep selector DSL limited: `type`: ["tenant", "tag", "percent"], `value`: string. Dont try to be a full policy language.

mira: Good call. Also: expiry semantics. Flags often represent transient signals (e.g., regression windows). Add `expires_at` and support tombstones.

liam: On performance: resolver lookup (model_ref + token) must be <5ms p95 in the common case. Timeline lookup should be optional for latency-critical paths. We can support a header `X-Redwood-Flags: prefer=none` to skip flag resolution on hot paths.

sofia: Also provide a fallback rule: if pointer falls back at runtime (e.g., canary unavailable -> stable), runtime must fetch the timeline for the fallback ref and annotate the response with which timeline was consulted. This is required for auditability.

mira: Regarding audit headers: propose `X-Redwood-Resolve: model=acme/qa@v3;ptr=99;tl=tl-20260305-00042`. Keep it short.

liam: Migration: existing pins will have inlined flags. We'll add a one-shot migration that pushes them to timeline entries and replaces the inlined blob with `pointer_id` reference. Migration steps must be reversible for 48 hours.

sofia: Legal/GDPR: timeline must support redact (hide content) and purge (delete entry). Redact keeps a tombstone entry with metadata `redacted=true` so audits show a record without sensitive content. Purge triggers an admin workflow with approval and is logged.

liam: Implementation detail: timeline entries schema should be flat strings (pointer_id, selector, flag_type, payload, created_at, expires_at, tombstone). Limit payload to 1KB as the RFC said. Keep everything string typed for storage simplicity.

mira: Compaction: periodic compactor should condense old timeline entries (older than retention window) into a single aggregated entry per pointer. This reduces read amplification for long-lived pointers. Compaction must preserve monotonic `timeline_token` semantics.

sofia: Quotas: add per-tenant write quotas for timeline writes and a per-pointer cap. Emit metrics: `timeline_writes`, `timeline_read_latency_ms`, `flags_per_pointer`.

liam: Tests: unit tests for selector evaluation (edge cases for percentage rollout), integration tests for resolver atomicity (race where pointer changes mid-request), and perf tests for resolver p50/p95 under cache hit/miss.

mira: API surfaces to draft: (A) Control-plane: create pointer, attach timeline entry, redact/purge, bulk-delete; (B) Runtime resolver: `GET /resolve?tenant=...&model=...` -> `{model_ref, pointer_id, timeline_token}`; (C) Timeline fetch: `GET /timeline?pointer_id=...&tenant=...&token=...` -> list of flags.

liam: Suggestion: make timeline fetch accept `token` as a read-since cursor to support incremental reads in the runtime. That helps streaming consumers and reduces payload.

sofia: Observability: include which timeline token served a response in traces and span attributes. Add an internal dashboard for stale timeline tokens and pointer-token divergence events.

mira: Security: timeline writes must require tenant-scoped auth and admin operations require separate scope. Also log who performed redactions/purges.

devops-bot: scheduled_task: "timeline-compaction" next_run=3332164000 status=scheduled

liam: Action items: I'll draft the resolver proto + cache invalidation rule. Aim for OpenAPI + example headers.

sofia: I'll write the selector DSL doc + tests and spec quotas/compactor cadence.

mira: I'll update the RFC with the append-only timeline model, redact/purge paths, migration plan, and the audit header pattern.

liam: One UX note: allow a control-plane preview API that returns what flags a tenant will see given a pointer/token. Useful for canary owners.

sofia: +1. Also add a small CLI tool for admins to diff pointer vs timeline state before migration runs.

mira: Great. Let's keep the resolver contract tiny and cache-friendly. I'll put a checklist in the RFC for all the invariants we discussed (monotonic tokens, eventual-consistency, redact vs purge, compaction guarantees).

liam: Cool. Target design PR by EOW.

sofia: I'll stub the compaction job in ops playbook.

devops-bot: note: design_board ticket created https://redwood.svc/t/DB-2910 :white_check_mark:

mira: Thanks. If no objections I'll fold this into the RFC follow-up doc tonight and ping the group.
